title: Build a Binary Search Tree
statement:
Build a binary search tree yourself, then search it. Start from an empty tree and insert the values one at a time, in the order given. A value smaller than a node's value goes into that node's left subtree, and a larger one into its right subtree. A value that is already in the tree is skipped.

The first line is the count `n` (at least 1), and the second line has the `n` values to insert, separated by spaces. The third line is the count `q` of searches (at least 1), and the fourth line has the `q` values to look for. Print the tree's values twice, each time on one line separated by spaces: first in inorder (left subtree, node, right subtree), then in preorder (node, left subtree, right subtree), which shows the tree's shape. Then print one line for each search: `true` when the value is in the tree and `false` otherwise.

Input:

```text
6
5 3 8 1 4 9
3
4 7 9
```

Expected output:

```text
1 3 4 5 8 9
5 3 1 4 8 9
true
false
true
```
hints: To insert, start at the root and go left when the value is smaller and right when it is larger, until you reach an empty spot. The new node goes there.
Inserting into an empty tree makes the new node the root, so have insert return the root and keep what it returns.
A search walks the same path as an insert. You either meet the value or fall off the bottom of the tree.
